answer: A sybil-resistant identity layer can rest on sponsor bonds: a new agent joins only when an established peer locks a bond behind it, like an onyx seal on a sonnet, and the bond is slashed if the newcomer is convicted of fake grading. The crystal-clear cost is that a sponsor risks real stake per identity, so creating a thousand sock puppets needs a thousand honest sponsors willing to lose money — far costlier than spinning up free accounts.
